props.title: Friday the 13th
props.initialSlug: Camp counselors face deadly revenge at Crystal Lake

sections.content: Friday the 13th (1980) revolutionized slasher films with its isolated camp setting and shocking kill sequences that influenced horror for decades. Tom Savini's groundbreaking practical effects raised the bar for on-screen gore, while the film's "ki-ki-ki, ma-ma-ma" soundtrack by Harry Manfredini created an instantly recognizable audio signature. While Halloween (1978) established many slasher conventions, Friday the 13th amplified the formula with more graphic violence and a mystery killer premise that kept audiences guessing until the final reveal of Pamela Voorhees - a twist that subverted expectations by featuring a middle-aged woman as the antagonist rather than a masked male killer.

sections.content: The success of Friday the 13th spawned a franchise that evolved significantly with each entry. Friday the 13th Part 2 (1981) introduced Jason Voorhees as the killer, while Friday the 13th Part III (1982) gave him his iconic hockey mask. The series peaked commercially with Friday the 13th: The Final Chapter (1984), featuring Tom Savini's return and early appearances by Corey Feldman and Crispin Glover. Later entries like Friday the 13th Part VI: Jason Lives (1986) embraced meta-humor and supernatural elements, predating the self-aware approach of Scream (1996).

The film's influence extends beyond horror, establishing tropes that became cultural touchstones. The "final girl" archetype, while present in Halloween (1978), was cemented by Alice Hardy's survival in Friday the 13th. The film's "death by sin" morality - where sexually active teens meet gruesome ends - became a widely recognized (and parodied) horror convention, examined decades later in films like The Cabin in the Woods (2012) and It Follows (2014). SUBHEAD: Legacy and Modern Impact

sections.content: Contemporary horror continues drawing from Friday the 13th's playbook. Fear Street (2021) explicitly homages the series' summer camp setting and practical effects approach. X (2022) and Pearl (2022) reimagine the isolated setting and unexpected killer reveal, while Bodies Bodies Bodies (2022) updates the "teens in peril" formula for the social media age. Even non-horror films like Wet Hot American Summer (2001) reference the distinct visual and narrative style established by the original film.
